The tree was empty, so this revision seeds it. Nothing could be rolled up because there are no results yet. It adds 3 open Lvl1 hypotheses, each split into mechanisms (Lvl2) and numbered predictions (Lvl3): - **A, sample efficiency (epochs needed to hit target).** Its main mechanism is a port of airbench, Keller Jordan's fast CIFAR-10 training recipe, with TTA (test-time augmentation) removed. A public 8.11 s / 75.29% result on this same benchmark makes it the obvious starting point. That result comes only from search snippets; the code itself wasn't verified. Other mechanisms under A:   - alternating flip   - label smoothing 0.3 and no Cutout at short schedules   - SGD vs Muon   - the trade-off between width and epochs   - dropping easy examples late in training - **B, per-step throughput.** Mechanisms:   - GPU-resident data, since only 4 CPU cores are available   - channels_last + fp16 + compiling during the untimed build   - progressive resizing - **C, fixed overhead in the timed window.** Mechanisms:   - whitening init from a subset, plus one bulk transfer to the GPU   - zero recompiles during training, plus a safe eval path for every batch size The review's methodology points are now concrete predictions: - **Noise model (A1c):** the minimum accuracy and time differences that count as real, so smaller deltas are treated as inconclusive. - **TTA ban (A1b):** losing TTA leaves under 0.3 pp of margin at 8.5 epochs, so about one more epoch is probably needed. - **Recompile and eval checks (C2a):** zero recompiles in the timed region, and finite logits within 5 s for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Recommended first steps: 1. Run the unmodified template, with prepare, train and per-epoch time logged separately. 2. Run the airbench port (A1a), then repeat it to get the noise estimate. Treat any result between 0.753 and about 0.756 as provisional, because of selection bias near the cutoff. Times measured on the SXM card won't transfer exactly to the PCIe judging GPU.

added I035, I036, I037, I038, I039, I040; dropped none. The queue had no queued ideas left, so I added 6 (4 exploit, 2 explore). The binding constraint is margin: pooling E025 and its salted re-run (E027) puts the incumbent's expected accuracy at about 0.7533, right at the 0.753 bar. Accuracy deltas are judged against that pooled figure, not E025's single draw of 0.7539. 1. **Muon lr 1.25x (H1.7.6), priority 5.** A free accuracy gain is the most valuable result now. The rationale is that Turbo preconditioning shrank the effective update by about a third. 2. **Whitening bias trained only in the 24 px phase, then detached (H2.4.4), priority 4.** This removes work in the 28/32 px phases and needs no extra graph. Expected time -1 to -2% with accuracy unchanged. 3. **20 px for the first 2 epochs (H2.3), priority 3.** Extends the resolution ladder. Expected -3 to -4% time for about -0.15 pp; pair it with any margin gain. 4. **Batch 3072 in the 24 px phase only (H2.3.3), priority 2.** Halves the fixed Muon cost per low-res step. Riskier for accuracy. 5. **+0.5 epoch at 32 px (H1.8.1), priority 2.** Measures the pp/s slope and gives a safe fallback config. It won't beat E025 on time, so it is calibration only. 6. **Label smoothing 0.4 (H1.3.1), priority 2.** The last untested direction of that knob; time-neutral. No queued ideas needed dropping. I left H1.2.1 alone because alternating flip is already in the recipe, and skipped H1.6.2 and H2.4.3 because their priors are weak. H4.3 (dev seeds) isn't a file change, so it can't be an idea here.
